title: The Three Kingdoms
content_zh:
After Red Cliffs, China split into three realms: Wei under Cao Cao, Shu under Liu Bei, and Wu under Sun Quan. What followed was a century of war, strategy, betrayal, and legend.
Zhuge Liang led six northern campaigns against Wei, crossing the treacherous Qishan Mountains again and again, pushing his frail body beyond its limits. In his final campaign, knowing he was dying, he left a wooden statue of himself at the command tent to deter the Wei forces.
Guan Yu met his tragic end at Fan Castle, ambushed by Wu forces. He faced his death with the same dignity with which he had lived. 'When the jade shatters, its splinters still kill,' he said before the sword fell.
Liu Bei, consumed by grief and rage, led a disastrous campaign against Wu to avenge his brother. He died soon after at White Emperor City, entrusting his son and his kingdom to Zhuge Liang.
In the end, none of the three kingdoms survived. The Sima family absorbed them all and founded the Jin Dynasty. The oath of the peach garden, the blood spilled, the strategies written — all became the lore of a nation.
